criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: Rebuilt the Command Center as a 9-tab app that fetches .colaberry/plan.json, progress.json and manifest.json at runtime (no bundler, no hard-coded project data). Verified in a real browser via Playwright: all 9 tabs reachable, drill-down works, SAMPLE label shows on every tab in sample mode, data-age banner with stale warning shows on every tab, and no tab ever renders a fabricated connection/run-history/points value.

criteria.text: Given a client profile, purchase history, and preferences, When the system analyzes the data, Then it identifies the strongest clienteling opportunity.
Given incomplete client data, When the system attempts analysis, Then it provides a meaningful error message.
Trust: The system logs the reasoning for each opportunity identified.

stories.notes: Implemented a deterministic opportunity-detection algorithm: validateClientData enforces the required shape (client id/name, preferences, purchaseHistory entries, lastContactedOn) and returns a field-specific error on anything missing or malformed; scoreOpportunities scores each catalog product against the client's preferred categories/houses, new-arrival status, category-expansion, and spend alignment, plus a re-engagement candidate once the contact gap passes 60 days; identifyOpportunity picks the highest-scoring candidate deterministically and calls logOpportunityReasoning to append it (with its full reasoning) to an in-memory audit log exposed via getOpportunityAuditLog. Sample data is fictional only (src/sampleClients.ts, src/sampleProducts.ts). All 44 test files / 145 tests pass via `npm test`; `tsc --noEmit` is clean; every new src file has a matching test and stays under 200 lines.

criteria.text: Given an identified opportunity, When the system generates a message, Then the message is personalized and editable.
Given an invalid opportunity, When the system attempts to generate a message, Then it provides a meaningful error message.
Trust: The system logs all generated messages for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Implemented message generation on top of an identified opportunity: findMessageTemplate (messageTemplates.ts) maps an opportunity type to a subject/body template and fails gracefully on an unrecognized type; generateMessage (generateMessage.ts) validates the opportunity (present, belongs to the given client, product resolves in the catalog when the template requires one), fills the template's {{clientName}}/{{productName}}/{{productHouse}}/{{preferredCategory}} placeholders, and returns an editable OutreachMessage (plain mutable fields, no auto-send path) or a meaningful error; every successful generation is appended to an in-memory audit log via logMessageGeneration.ts, mirroring the STORY-001 opportunity audit log. 48 test files / 164 tests pass via `npm test`; `tsc --noEmit` is clean; every new src file has a matching test and stays under 200 lines.

criteria.text: Given an identified opportunity, When the system recommends a product, Then the product is relevant to the client's preferences.
Given no available products, When the system attempts to recommend, Then it provides a meaningful error message.
Trust: The system logs the reasoning for each product recommendation.

stories.notes: Implemented product recommendation on top of an identified opportunity: recommendProduct (recommendProduct.ts) validates the opportunity/client pair, rejects a catalog that is not loaded or empty with a meaningful error, scores every catalog product against the client's preferred categories/houses/new-arrival status, and returns the best-scoring match (or a meaningful error naming the client when nothing scores above zero) with its reasoning trail (productRecommendation.ts). Every successful recommendation is appended to an in-memory audit log via logProductRecommendation.ts, mirroring the STORY-001/STORY-002 audit logs. Deliberately independent of the productId that identifyOpportunity may already attach, since this is its own auditable recommendation. Two listed failure paths (AI model fails to recommend / recommendation timeout) are not applicable: this codebase uses deterministic, synchronous scoring rather than an external AI call, consistent with STORY-001/STORY-002 — confirmed with the user before implementing. 51 test files / 178 tests pass via `npm test`; every new src file has a matching test and stays under 200 lines (13/24/93 lines).

criteria.text: Given the system is running, When an advisor logs in, Then they see a user-friendly interface.
Given a UI component fails to load, When an advisor accesses the system, Then a fallback UI is displayed.
Trust: The system logs all advisor interactions with the UI.

stories.notes: New advisor-facing dashboard (advisor.html), separate from the STORY-000 Command Center. Roster -> client detail view runs the existing identifyOpportunity -> recommendProduct -> generateMessage pipeline, with an editable message draft and a queue-for-approval action (no send capability exists anywhere in the codebase). Component crashes and missing data render fallback/empty-state UI instead of blank panels or exceptions. All advisor navigation, message edits, and queue actions are recorded via logAdvisorInteraction. Queueing is UI-only in-memory state for now; persistence is STORY-005.
